drug_profiles.name: Trifluridine/tipiracil
drug_profiles.drug_class: Thymidine-based nucleoside analogue with thymidine phosphorylase inhibitor
drug_profiles.mechanism: Trifluridine is incorporated into DNA and disrupts DNA function. Tipiracil inhibits thymidine phosphorylase, increasing systemic exposure to trifluridine.

drug_profiles.name: Fluorouracil
drug_profiles.mechanism: Intracellular metabolites inhibit thymidylate synthase and can be incorporated into RNA and DNA, disrupting nucleic-acid synthesis and function.

drug_profiles.name: Folinic acid
drug_profiles.mechanism: Stabilises the fluorouracil–thymidylate synthase complex, enhancing fluorouracil-mediated inhibition of thymidylate synthesis. It is not itself a cytotoxic component in these regimens.

drug_profiles.name: Oxaliplatin
drug_profiles.mechanism: Forms platinum–DNA adducts and cross-links that interfere with DNA replication and transcription, leading to cell death.

drug_profiles.name: Irinotecan
drug_profiles.mechanism: Its active metabolite SN-38 stabilises the topoisomerase I–DNA complex, preventing repair of single-strand breaks during DNA replication.

drug_profiles.name: Durvalumab
drug_profiles.mechanism: Binds PD-L1 and blocks its interaction with PD-1 and CD80, supporting restoration of antitumour T-cell activity.

drug_profiles.name: Pembrolizumab
drug_profiles.mechanism: Binds PD-1 and blocks interaction with PD-L1 and PD-L2, reducing inhibitory signalling in activated T cells.

drug_profiles.name: Nivolumab
drug_profiles.mechanism: Binds PD-1 and blocks ligand-mediated inhibitory signalling, supporting antitumour T-cell responses.

drug_profiles.name: Atezolizumab
drug_profiles.mechanism: Binds PD-L1 and blocks interactions with PD-1 and CD80, reducing checkpoint-mediated suppression of T-cell activity.

drug_profiles.name: Pemetrexed
drug_profiles.mechanism: Inhibits folate-dependent enzymes involved in purine and thymidylate synthesis, impairing DNA and RNA synthesis.

drug_profiles.name: Carboplatin
drug_profiles.mechanism: Forms platinum–DNA adducts and cross-links that disrupt DNA replication and transcription.

drug_profiles.name: Paclitaxel
drug_profiles.mechanism: Promotes microtubule assembly and prevents normal microtubule disassembly, disrupting mitosis and intracellular transport.

drug_profiles.name: Docetaxel
drug_profiles.mechanism: Stabilises microtubules and inhibits their depolymerisation, causing disruption of mitotic and cellular functions.

drug_profiles.name: Doxorubicin
drug_profiles.mechanism: Intercalates into DNA, inhibits topoisomerase II and generates reactive species, causing DNA damage and impaired replication.

drug_profiles.name: Pegylated liposomal doxorubicin
drug_profiles.mechanism: Delivers doxorubicin in a pegylated liposomal formulation. Released doxorubicin intercalates DNA and inhibits topoisomerase II.

drug_profiles.name: Cyclophosphamide
drug_profiles.mechanism: Hepatic activation produces metabolites that form DNA cross-links, interfering with DNA replication and cell division.

drug_profiles.name: Trastuzumab
drug_profiles.mechanism: Binds the extracellular domain of HER2, inhibiting signalling and promoting immune-mediated destruction of HER2-expressing tumour cells.

drug_profiles.name: Pertuzumab
drug_profiles.mechanism: Binds a different extracellular HER2 domain from trastuzumab and inhibits ligand-dependent HER2 dimerisation with other HER family receptors.

drug_profiles.name: Abemaciclib
drug_profiles.mechanism: Inhibits cyclin-dependent kinases 4 and 6, reducing retinoblastoma-protein phosphorylation and limiting progression from G1 to S phase.

drug_profiles.name: Bevacizumab
drug_profiles.mechanism: Binds VEGF-A and reduces activation of VEGF receptors, inhibiting tumour-associated angiogenic signalling.

drug_profiles.name: Gemcitabine
drug_profiles.mechanism: Active metabolites inhibit ribonucleotide reductase and are incorporated into DNA, impairing DNA synthesis.

drug_profiles.name: Cisplatin
drug_profiles.mechanism: Forms intra- and inter-strand DNA cross-links that disrupt DNA replication and transcription.

drug_profiles.name: Axitinib
drug_profiles.mechanism: Inhibits VEGFR-1, VEGFR-2 and VEGFR-3 signalling, reducing angiogenesis and tumour vascular growth.

drug_profiles.name: Enfortumab vedotin
drug_profiles.drug_class: Nectin-4-directed antibody linked to a microtubule-disrupting payload
drug_profiles.mechanism: Binds Nectin-4, is internalised and releases monomethyl auristatin E, which disrupts microtubules and induces cell death.

drug_profiles.name: Sacituzumab govitecan
drug_profiles.mechanism: Binds Trop-2 on tumour cells and delivers SN-38, the active metabolite of irinotecan. SN-38 inhibits topoisomerase I, producing DNA damage during replication; released payload may also affect nearby tumour cells.
drug_profiles.review_status: Draft — consultant and oncology-pharmacy review pending

drug_profiles.name: Capecitabine
drug_profiles.mechanism: Converted through enzymatic steps to fluorouracil, which inhibits thymidylate synthase and disrupts RNA and DNA synthesis. The oral schedule creates repeated systemic fluoropyrimidine exposure while retaining the same DPD-dependent toxicity mechanism as fluorouracil.
drug_profiles.review_status: Draft — consultant oncology and oncology-pharmacy review pending

drug_profiles.name: Trastuzumab deruxtecan
drug_profiles.drug_class: HER2-directed antibody linked to a topoisomerase-I inhibitor payload
drug_profiles.mechanism: The trastuzumab component binds HER2 and promotes internalisation. Lysosomal cleavage releases a membrane-permeable deruxtecan topoisomerase-I inhibitor payload, producing DNA damage in the target cell and a potential bystander effect in adjacent tumour cells.
drug_profiles.review_status: Draft — consultant oncology and oncology-pharmacy review pending

drug_profiles.name: Ipilimumab
drug_profiles.mechanism: Binds CTLA 4 and reduces inhibitory signalling during T cell priming, supporting broader antitumour T cell activation.

drug_profiles.name: Prednisolone
drug_profiles.mechanism: Activates glucocorticoid receptors and modifies inflammatory and transcriptional signalling. In the established docetaxel prostate regimen it is given continuously as part of the treatment schedule.

drug_profiles.name: Avelumab
drug_profiles.mechanism: Binds PD L1 and blocks interaction with PD 1 and B7.1, reducing inhibitory signalling that limits antitumour T cell activity.

drug_profiles.name: Osimertinib
drug_profiles.drug_class: Third generation EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor
drug_profiles.mechanism: Irreversibly inhibits sensitising and T790M mutant EGFR signalling while having lower activity against wild type EGFR than earlier generation inhibitors.

drug_profiles.name: Olaparib
drug_profiles.mechanism: Inhibits PARP mediated DNA repair and traps PARP on damaged DNA, creating selective vulnerability in tumours with homologous recombination repair defects such as BRCA1 or BRCA2 loss.

drug_profiles.name: Etoposide
drug_profiles.mechanism: Stabilises the transient DNA topoisomerase II cleavage complex, causing double strand DNA breaks and inhibition of DNA replication.

drug_profiles.name: Dabrafenib
drug_profiles.mechanism: Inhibits activated BRAF kinase, including BRAF V600 mutant signalling, reducing downstream MAPK pathway activity and tumour cell proliferation.

drug_profiles.name: Trametinib
drug_profiles.mechanism: Allosterically inhibits MEK1 and MEK2 activation and kinase activity, suppressing downstream ERK signalling within the MAPK pathway.

evidence_records.publication_title: Randomized Trial of TAS-102 for Refractory Metastatic Colorectal Cancer
evidence_records.evidence_context: Previously treated metastatic colorectal cancer
evidence_records.relevance_summary: Supports trifluridine/tipiracil in refractory metastatic colorectal cancer after standard therapies.
evidence_records.limitations: Placebo-controlled later-line population. The publication supports trifluridine/tipiracil monotherapy and does not itself establish a trifluridine/tipiracil plus bevacizumab protocol.
evidence_records.match_type: Exact medicine, schedule family and disease setting
evidence_records.trial_population: 800 patients with metastatic colorectal cancer refractory to, or intolerant of, standard therapies.
key_findings: Median overall survival was 7.1 months versus 5.3 months; hazard ratio for death 0.68.
Median progression-free survival was 2.0 months versus 1.7 months; hazard ratio 0.48.

evidence_records.publication_title: Trifluridine–Tipiracil and Bevacizumab in Refractory Metastatic Colorectal Cancer
evidence_records.evidence_context: Refractory metastatic colorectal cancer after two previous chemotherapy regimens
evidence_records.study_design: International phase 3 randomised open-label active-controlled trial
evidence_records.trial_population: 492 adults with refractory metastatic colorectal cancer after two previous chemotherapy regimens.
key_findings: Median overall survival was 10.8 months with trifluridine/tipiracil plus bevacizumab versus 7.5 months with trifluridine/tipiracil alone; hazard ratio for death 0.61.
Median progression-free survival was 5.6 months versus 2.4 months; hazard ratio for progression or death 0.44.
evidence_records.relevance_summary: Shows improved survival from adding bevacizumab to trifluridine/tipiracil in refractory metastatic colorectal cancer.
evidence_records.limitations: Contextual combination evidence only. The currently encoded NCCP 00382 protocol is trifluridine/tipiracil monotherapy, and SACTCheck does not infer a combined prescribing or dose-modification pathway from SUNLIGHT.
evidence_records.match_type: Exact disease and trifluridine/tipiracil medicine match; treatment combination differs from the encoded NCCP protocol
evidence_records.review_status: Draft — consultant oncology and oncology-pharmacy review pending

evidence_records.publication_title: Pembrolizumab plus Chemotherapy in Metastatic Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer
evidence_records.evidence_context: Previously untreated metastatic non-squamous NSCLC without EGFR or ALK alterations
evidence_records.relevance_summary: Supports pembrolizumab with pemetrexed and platinum chemotherapy in the specified first-line metastatic non-squamous NSCLC setting.
evidence_records.limitations: KEYNOTE-189 allowed cisplatin or carboplatin, whereas this NCCP protocol specifies carboplatin. The current NCCP schedule and eligibility criteria remain authoritative.
evidence_records.match_type: Exact immunotherapy and pemetrexed-platinum strategy; platinum selection narrowed locally
evidence_records.trial_population: 616 patients with previously untreated metastatic non-squamous NSCLC without sensitising EGFR or ALK alterations.
evidence_records.intervention: Pembrolizumab plus pemetrexed and platinum chemotherapy, followed by protocol-defined maintenance treatment.
evidence_records.comparator: Placebo plus pemetrexed and platinum chemotherapy.
key_findings: Estimated 12-month overall survival was 69.2% versus 49.4%; hazard ratio for death 0.49.
Median progression-free survival was 8.8 months versus 4.9 months; hazard ratio 0.52.
At 5 years, overall survival was 19.4% versus 11.3% in the updated analysis.

supporting_publications.label: Five-year outcomes
supporting_publications.title: Pembrolizumab Plus Pemetrexed and Platinum in Nonsquamous Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer: 5-Year Outcomes From the Phase 3 KEYNOTE-189 Study

evidence_records.publication_title: Durvalumab after Chemoradiotherapy in Stage III Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer
evidence_records.evidence_context: Unresectable stage III NSCLC without progression after concurrent chemoradiotherapy
evidence_records.relevance_summary: Supports consolidation durvalumab following definitive concurrent chemoradiotherapy in the studied stage III NSCLC population.
evidence_records.limitations: The PACIFIC trial used weight-based dosing every 2 weeks. The current NCCP protocol uses 1500 mg every 28 days and applies current European and local eligibility criteria, including PD-L1 requirements.
evidence_records.match_type: Exact treatment strategy and disease setting; administration schedule differs
evidence_records.trial_population: 713 patients with unresectable stage III NSCLC without progression after concurrent platinum-based chemoradiotherapy.
evidence_records.intervention: Durvalumab 10 mg/kg every 2 weeks for up to 12 months.
evidence_records.comparator: Placebo every 2 weeks for up to 12 months.
key_findings: Median progression-free survival was 16.8 months versus 5.6 months; hazard ratio 0.52 in the initial analysis.
The 24-month overall-survival rate was 66.3% versus 55.6%; hazard ratio for death 0.68.
Estimated 5-year overall survival was 42.9% versus 33.4% in the updated analysis.

supporting_publications.title: Overall Survival with Durvalumab after Chemoradiotherapy in Stage III NSCLC

evidence_records.publication_title: Pembrolizumab for Early Triple-Negative Breast Cancer
evidence_records.evidence_context: High-risk early triple-negative breast cancer
evidence_records.relevance_summary: Supports neoadjuvant pembrolizumab with chemotherapy followed by adjuvant pembrolizumab in high-risk early triple-negative breast cancer.
evidence_records.limitations: The full treatment sequence, phase-specific chemotherapy details and eligibility criteria must be checked against the current NCCP protocol. Evidence outcomes apply to the complete perioperative strategy rather than an isolated phase.
evidence_records.match_type: Exact perioperative treatment strategy; current phase schedule encoded separately
evidence_records.trial_population: 1174 patients with previously untreated stage II or III triple-negative breast cancer.
evidence_records.intervention: Neoadjuvant pembrolizumab plus platinum-containing chemotherapy, followed by surgery and adjuvant pembrolizumab.
evidence_records.comparator: Matched placebo plus neoadjuvant chemotherapy, followed by surgery and adjuvant placebo.
evidence_records.primary_endpoint: Pathological complete response and event-free survival; overall survival was subsequently reported.
key_findings: Pathological complete response was 64.8% versus 51.2% at the first interim analysis.
Estimated 36-month event-free survival was 84.5% versus 76.8%; hazard ratio 0.63.
Estimated 60-month overall survival was 86.6% versus 81.7% in the later analysis.

supporting_publications.title: Event-free Survival with Pembrolizumab in Early Triple-Negative Breast Cancer

supporting_publications.title: Overall Survival with Pembrolizumab in Early-Stage Triple-Negative Breast Cancer

evidence_records.publication_title: Pegylated Liposomal Doxorubicin and Carboplatin Compared with Paclitaxel and Carboplatin for Patients with Platinum-Sensitive Ovarian Cancer in Late Relapse
evidence_records.evidence_context: Platinum-sensitive recurrent ovarian cancer, mapped to the related NCCP ovarian, fallopian-tube and primary-peritoneal protocol.
evidence_records.relevance_summary: Supports carboplatin plus pegylated liposomal doxorubicin in platinum-sensitive recurrent ovarian cancer.
evidence_records.limitations: The comparator was carboplatin plus paclitaxel and the trial population had platinum-sensitive recurrence. Individual suitability and all current treatment criteria remain governed by the NCCP protocol.
evidence_records.match_type: Exact component combination, dose schedule and recurrent disease setting
evidence_records.trial_population: 976 patients with platinum-sensitive relapsed or recurrent ovarian cancer more than 6 months after prior platinum and taxane treatment.
evidence_records.intervention: Carboplatin AUC 5 plus pegylated liposomal doxorubicin 30 mg/m² every 4 weeks.
evidence_records.comparator: Carboplatin AUC 5 plus paclitaxel 175 mg/m² every 3 weeks.
key_findings: Median progression-free survival was 11.3 months versus 9.4 months; hazard ratio 0.821.
The carboplatin and pegylated liposomal doxorubicin arm had less alopecia, hypersensitivity and sensory neuropathy, but more hand-foot syndrome, nausea and mucositis.
Final overall survival was similar between treatment groups.

supporting_publications.label: Final overall-survival analysis
supporting_publications.title: Final overall survival results of phase III GCIG CALYPSO trial of pegylated liposomal doxorubicin and carboplatin vs paclitaxel and carboplatin in platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer patients

evidence_records.publication_title: FOLFIRI followed by FOLFOX6 or the reverse sequence in advanced colorectal cancer
evidence_records.evidence_context: First-line and sequential treatment of metastatic colorectal cancer
evidence_records.trial_population: Patients with previously untreated metastatic colorectal cancer.
evidence_records.intervention: FOLFIRI followed by FOLFOX6 at progression.
evidence_records.comparator: FOLFOX6 followed by FOLFIRI at progression.
key_findings: Both treatment sequences produced similar overall survival and allowed most patients to receive both active backbones.
The study supports FOLFOX6 as an active metastatic colorectal regimen and its sequencing with FOLFIRI.
evidence_records.relevance_summary: Adds disease-specific evidence for the metastatic colorectal indication in the shared mFOLFOX-6 protocol.
evidence_records.limitations: This was a sequencing study and did not test the exact current supportive-care or dose-modification framework.
evidence_records.match_type: Exact FOLFOX6 regimen family and disease setting
evidence_records.review_status: Draft — consultant oncology and oncology-pharmacy review pending

evidence_records.publication_title: Oxaliplatin, Fluorouracil, and Leucovorin as Adjuvant Treatment for Colon Cancer
evidence_records.evidence_context: Adjuvant colon cancer
evidence_records.relevance_summary: Established the clinical value of adding oxaliplatin to fluorouracil and folinic acid in adjuvant colon cancer.
evidence_records.limitations: The trial used FOLFOX4 rather than the exact modified FOLFOX-6 schedule and does not cover every indication listed in the shared NCCP protocol.
evidence_records.match_type: Regimen-family evidence; schedule differs
evidence_records.review_status: Draft — consultant and oncology-pharmacy review pending
evidence_records.trial_population: 2246 patients with completely resected stage II or III colon cancer.
evidence_records.intervention: FOLFOX4: oxaliplatin plus infusional and bolus fluorouracil with folinic acid every 2 weeks for 12 cycles.
evidence_records.comparator: LV5FU2 fluorouracil and folinic acid without oxaliplatin.
key_findings: Three-year disease-free survival was 78.2% with FOLFOX4 versus 72.9% with LV5FU2; hazard ratio 0.77.
At 10 years, overall survival was 71.7% versus 67.1% in the overall stage II/III population; the clearest overall-survival benefit was in stage III disease.

supporting_publications.label: Ten-year outcomes
supporting_publications.title: Adjuvant Fluorouracil, Leucovorin, and Oxaliplatin in Stage II to III Colon Cancer: Updated 10-Year Survival and Outcomes According to BRAF Mutation and Mismatch Repair Status of the MOSAIC Study

evidence_records.publication_title: Phase III trial of fluorouracil, leucovorin plus either oxaliplatin or cisplatin in advanced gastric cancer
evidence_records.evidence_context: First-line advanced gastric or gastro-oesophageal-junction adenocarcinoma
evidence_records.trial_population: Patients with untreated advanced gastric adenocarcinoma.
key_findings: Oxaliplatin-based therapy produced at least comparable efficacy with a different toxicity profile from cisplatin-based therapy.
The trial supports an oxaliplatin–infusional-fluorouracil backbone in advanced gastric cancer.
evidence_records.relevance_summary: Adds upper-GI evidence for the advanced gastric/GEJ indication in the shared protocol.
evidence_records.limitations: FLO is not identical to the encoded modified FOLFOX-6 doses and sequence.
evidence_records.match_type: Disease and drug-backbone evidence; schedule differs

evidence_records.publication_title: Duration of Adjuvant Chemotherapy for Stage III Colon Cancer
evidence_records.evidence_context: Duration of oxaliplatin-based adjuvant chemotherapy in stage III colon cancer
evidence_records.study_design: Prospective pooled analysis of six randomised phase 3 trials
evidence_records.trial_population: 12,834 patients with stage III colon cancer assigned to 3 or 6 months of FOLFOX or CAPOX.
evidence_records.intervention: Three months of oxaliplatin-based adjuvant therapy.
evidence_records.comparator: Six months of oxaliplatin-based adjuvant therapy.
key_findings: Non-inferiority of 3 months versus 6 months was not established in the overall pooled population.
The regimen and clinical-risk interactions support individualised duration decisions rather than a single duration for every patient.
evidence_records.relevance_summary: Provides treatment-duration context for adjuvant oxaliplatin/fluoropyrimidine regimens.
evidence_records.limitations: This pooled analysis combines FOLFOX and CAPOX and should not be used as a stand-alone patient-specific duration rule.
evidence_records.match_type: Practice-changing duration evidence
evidence_records.review_status: Draft — consultant oncology and oncology-pharmacy review pending

evidence_records.evidence_context: Metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma
evidence_records.relevance_summary: Closes the metastatic-indication gap in the shared modified FOLFIRINOX knowledge profile.
evidence_records.limitations: The trial used the original FOLFIRINOX schedule. The encoded NCCP protocol is modified FOLFIRINOX, so dose intensity and toxicity are not an exact schedule match.

evidence_records.publication_title: FOLFIRINOX or Gemcitabine as Adjuvant Therapy for Pancreatic Cancer
evidence_records.evidence_context: Adjuvant treatment after resection of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
evidence_records.relevance_summary: Supports modified FOLFIRINOX in the adjuvant pancreatic-cancer setting.
evidence_records.limitations: The NCCP protocol also includes metastatic treatment; this publication specifically supports the adjuvant context.
evidence_records.match_type: Exact modified regimen in adjuvant context
evidence_records.review_status: Draft — consultant and oncology-pharmacy review pending

evidence_records.publication_title: Efficacy and safety of neoadjuvant pertuzumab and trastuzumab in women with locally advanced, inflammatory, or early HER2-positive breast cancer
evidence_records.evidence_context: Neoadjuvant dual-HER2 blockade
evidence_records.trial_population: 417 women with HER2-positive locally advanced, inflammatory or early breast cancer.
evidence_records.intervention: Pertuzumab, trastuzumab and docetaxel in the relevant treatment arm.
evidence_records.comparator: Trastuzumab and docetaxel, with additional experimental arms.
evidence_records.primary_endpoint: Pathological complete response in the breast.
key_findings: Adding pertuzumab to trastuzumab and docetaxel increased pathological complete response compared with trastuzumab and docetaxel alone.
Five-year follow-up supported the prognostic relationship between pathological response and longer-term outcomes.
evidence_records.relevance_summary: Supports the contribution of pertuzumab to neoadjuvant dual-HER2 blockade.
evidence_records.limitations: NeoSphere did not use the full carboplatin-containing TCHP schedule. TRYPHAENA remains the closer anthracycline-free TCHP safety and activity mapping.
evidence_records.match_type: Component-strategy evidence; chemotherapy backbone differs
evidence_records.review_status: Draft — consultant oncology and oncology-pharmacy review pending

supporting_publications.title: 5-year analysis of neoadjuvant pertuzumab and trastuzumab in patients with HER2-positive breast cancer (NeoSphere)

evidence_records.publication_title: Pertuzumab plus Trastuzumab in Combination with Standard Neoadjuvant Anthracycline-Containing and Anthracycline-Free Chemotherapy Regimens in Patients with HER2-Positive Early Breast Cancer
evidence_records.evidence_context: Neoadjuvant HER2-positive early or locally advanced breast cancer
evidence_records.relevance_summary: Included an anthracycline-free docetaxel, carboplatin, trastuzumab and pertuzumab cohort relevant to TCHP.
evidence_records.limitations: The study was phase 2 and designed primarily around cardiac safety rather than a definitive comparative efficacy endpoint.
evidence_records.match_type: Exact component combination in a trial cohort
evidence_records.review_status: Draft — consultant and oncology-pharmacy review pending
evidence_records.trial_population: 225 patients with operable, locally advanced or inflammatory HER2-positive breast cancer.
evidence_records.intervention: Three neoadjuvant pertuzumab/trastuzumab-containing cohorts; arm C received docetaxel, carboplatin, trastuzumab and pertuzumab for 6 cycles.
evidence_records.comparator: No conventional control arm; three active regimens were evaluated primarily for cardiac safety.
evidence_records.primary_endpoint: Cardiac safety, including symptomatic left-ventricular systolic dysfunction and protocol-defined LVEF decline.
key_findings: Breast pathological complete response (ypT0/is) was 66.2% in the anthracycline-free TCHP cohort.
In the TCHP cohort, 3.9% had an LVEF decline of at least 10 percentage points to below 50% during neoadjuvant treatment; symptomatic LV systolic dysfunction was uncommon across the study.

evidence_records.evidence_context: High-risk node-positive HR-positive, HER2-negative early breast cancer
evidence_records.relevance_summary: Supports adding adjuvant abemaciclib to endocrine therapy in the trial-defined high-risk population.
evidence_records.limitations: Eligibility definitions and biomarker requirements have evolved; the current NCCP protocol is authoritative for present-day use.
evidence_records.match_type: Exact medicine and adjuvant setting

evidence_records.trial_population: 5637 patients with HR-positive, HER2-negative, node-positive early breast cancer at high risk of recurrence under the monarchE eligibility definitions.
evidence_records.intervention: Abemaciclib for 2 years plus clinician-selected standard adjuvant endocrine therapy.
key_findings: At the primary interim analysis, the hazard ratio for invasive disease-free survival was 0.75; 2-year IDFS was 92.2% versus 88.7%.
At 5 years, the absolute improvement was 7.6 percentage points for invasive disease-free survival and 6.7 percentage points for distant relapse-free survival.

evidence_records.limitations: Trial eligibility included liver-function and bleeding-risk criteria; current NCCP assessment and local hepatology pathways remain authoritative.

evidence_records.publication_title: Irinotecan Combined with Fluorouracil Compared with Fluorouracil Alone as First-Line Treatment for Metastatic Colorectal Cancer
evidence_records.evidence_context: First-line metastatic colorectal cancer
evidence_records.trial_population: 387 patients with previously untreated metastatic colorectal cancer.
evidence_records.intervention: Irinotecan combined with fluorouracil and folinic acid.
evidence_records.primary_endpoint: Response and time-to-progression outcomes, with overall survival assessed.
evidence_records.relevance_summary: Establishes the clinical contribution of adding irinotecan to a fluorouracil/folinic-acid backbone in metastatic colorectal cancer and supports the FOLFIRI treatment concept.
key_findings: Objective response was 49% with irinotecan plus fluorouracil/folinic acid versus 31% with fluorouracil/folinic acid alone.
Median time to progression was 6.7 versus 4.4 months, and median overall survival was 17.4 versus 14.1 months.
evidence_records.limitations: The trial is backbone evidence for metastatic colorectal cancer. NCCP 00227 also lists metastatic oesophageal and second-line pancreatic indications, and the trial does not validate those settings or every detail of the current local 14-day schedule.
evidence_records.match_type: Backbone evidence for the colorectal indication
evidence_records.review_status: Draft — consultant and oncology-pharmacy review pending

evidence_records.publication_title: FOLFIRI followed by FOLFOX6 or the reverse sequence in advanced colorectal cancer
evidence_records.evidence_context: First-line and sequential treatment of metastatic colorectal cancer
evidence_records.trial_population: Patients with previously untreated metastatic colorectal cancer.

regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Adjuvant high-risk stage I ovarian cancer; advanced ovarian, primary peritoneal or fallopian-tube cancer; selected endometrial, cervical and unknown-primary settings
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Paclitaxel stabilises microtubules and prevents normal mitotic spindle function. Carboplatin forms platinum–DNA cross-links; AUC-based dosing links exposure to renal clearance.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Paclitaxel 175 mg/m² over 3 hours followed by carboplatin AUC 5–7.5 over 30 minutes on day 1 every 21 days, generally for six cycles or until progression/unacceptable toxicity depending on the indication.
key_points: Multi-indication gynaecology protocol
Carboplatin dose depends on reliable GFR assessment
Paclitaxel premedication and hypersensitivity readiness are required
Neuropathy and cumulative marrow toxicity guide treatment

patient_selection.treatment_intent: Potentially curative adjuvant treatment in selected early-stage disease, or disease-control therapy in advanced/recurrent disease.
disease_and_biomarker_context: Confirm the exact gynaecological indication and planned carboplatin target AUC.
The GOG-158 evidence record is strongest for optimally resected stage III ovarian cancer and should not be treated as exact evidence for every protocol indication.
eligibility_orientation: Review ECOG status using the indication-specific protocol range.
Obtain FBC, renal and liver profile and a reliable GFR/CrCl assessment; measured GFR is preferred when feasible.
Assess baseline neuropathy, hearing where indicated, hypersensitivity history and pregnancy/breastfeeding exclusions.
important_cautions: Formula-derived GFR may overestimate function in obesity, low muscle mass or very low creatinine; use the protocol’s renal-dosing safeguards.
Severe hepatic impairment is an exclusion for paclitaxel, and baseline neutrophils below the protocol threshold require review.

supportive_care.emetogenic_risk: High because carboplatin AUC is at least 4; use the current high-risk antiemetic pathway.
premedication_and_prophylaxis: Give protocol-directed corticosteroid, H1-antihistamine and H2-antagonist premedication before paclitaxel, subject to consultant/local policy.
Ensure immediate access to anaphylaxis treatment.
Consider analgesic support for paclitaxel-associated myalgia/arthralgia.
patient_education: Report fever, rash, breathlessness or symptoms during/after infusion.
Report new numbness, pain, weakness or functional neuropathy before each cycle.
Explain that renal-function changes can alter the calculated carboplatin dose.
special_support: Review falls risk and function when neuropathy develops.
Coordinate audiometry and renal measurement when clinically indicated.

baseline: Measured GFR where feasible or protocol-approved GFR/CrCl estimation.
Peripheral-neuropathy assessment and audiometry when clinically indicated.
before_each_cycle: FBC with differential, renal and liver profile.
Current neuropathy grade and functional effect.
Previous hypersensitivity, thrombocytopenia, neutropenia or febrile neutropenia.
Recalculate carboplatin when renal function has materially changed, according to the protocol.
urgent_review_signals: Acute infusion reaction, wheeze, hypotension or angioedema
New motor neuropathy or function-limiting sensory neuropathy
Clinically important renal deterioration before AUC dosing

administration.cycle_and_sequence: Day 1 every 21 days: paclitaxel first, followed by carboplatin; typically six cycles or indication-directed continuation.
route_and_duration: Paclitaxel 175 mg/m² intravenously over 3 hours using non-PVC equipment and an in-line filter.
Carboplatin is administered intravenously over approximately 30 minutes at the selected AUC.
practical_workflow: Confirm target AUC and renal estimate used for the Calvert calculation.
Complete paclitaxel premedication and hypersensitivity checks before infusion.
Use the official protocol for renal caps, dose recalculation and hepatic paclitaxel adjustments.
observation_and_access: Monitor closely during paclitaxel, particularly early infusions.
Ensure resuscitation facilities are available throughout treatment.

regimen_profiles.regimen_role: First-line chemo-immunotherapy for metastatic squamous NSCLC
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Pembrolizumab plus paclitaxel and carboplatin combines PD-1 blockade with a platinum-taxane cytotoxic backbone for first-line metastatic squamous non-small-cell lung cancer, followed by pembrolizumab maintenance.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: First-line metastatic squamous non-small-cell lung cancer
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Pembrolizumab blocks PD-1-mediated immune inhibition. Paclitaxel disrupts microtubule function and mitosis, while carboplatin forms DNA cross-links. Cytotoxic tumour-cell killing and immune activation provide complementary antitumour effects.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Every 21 days: pembrolizumab 200 mg, paclitaxel 200 mg/m² and carboplatin AUC6 for four cycles, followed by pembrolizumab every 21 days until progression, unacceptable toxicity or the protocol-defined treatment limit.
key_points: First-line stage IV squamous NSCLC
Four induction cycles then pembrolizumab maintenance
High emetogenic risk from carboplatin AUC6
Separate immune-toxicity and cytotoxic-toxicity pathways

patient_selection.treatment_intent: Disease-control and survival-prolonging first-line systemic therapy.
disease_and_biomarker_context: Confirm histological or cytological stage IV squamous NSCLC.
Review molecular/pathological context and previous anti-PD-1/PD-L1 exposure according to the current protocol and treatment pathway.
KEYNOTE-407 demonstrated benefit across PD-L1 expression categories, but individual reimbursement and protocol criteria remain authoritative.
eligibility_orientation: ECOG 0–1 and adequate haematological, renal and hepatic function in the current protocol.
Review autoimmune disease, immunosuppression, unstable CNS metastases and prior severe immune toxicity.
Assess reliable GFR/CrCl for carboplatin and baseline neuropathy for paclitaxel.
important_cautions: Toxicity can arise from chemotherapy, immune activation or both; the mechanism should be considered before treatment decisions.
Paclitaxel- and carboplatin-related dose reductions do not automatically imply pembrolizumab dose reduction.

supportive_care.emetogenic_risk: High because carboplatin AUC6 is classified as high risk; pembrolizumab is minimal and paclitaxel low.
premedication_and_prophylaxis: Use the linked high-risk antiemetic pathway.
Give protocol-directed paclitaxel corticosteroid, H1 and H2 premedication.
Provide immune-toxicity education and an alert/contact pathway.
patient_education: Report fever, infusion symptoms and new neuropathy.
Report new cough, breathlessness, diarrhoea, rash, jaundice, endocrine symptoms, polyuria/polydipsia or marked fatigue promptly.
Explain that immune adverse events can occur during maintenance and after treatment ends.
special_support: Review smoking-related cardiopulmonary comorbidity and baseline oxygenation when clinically relevant.
Coordinate endocrinology, respiratory or other specialty review for suspected immune toxicity.

baseline: FBC, renal and liver profile and a protocol-appropriate GFR assessment.
Glucose, thyroid function and hepatitis screening.
Neuropathy, hearing and autoimmune/immune-toxicity baseline assessment as indicated.
before_each_cycle: FBC, renal and liver profile and glucose.
Thyroid function at the protocol-defined interval.
Screen for pneumonitis, colitis, hepatitis, endocrine, renal, neurological, cardiac and cutaneous immune toxicity.
Assess neuropathy, cytopenias, hypersensitivity and current chemotherapy dose levels during induction.
priority_toxicities: Immune endocrine, renal, cardiac, neurological and severe cutaneous toxicity
urgent_review_signals: New hypoxia, breathlessness or chest pain
Severe diarrhoea, jaundice or marked biochemical change
Adrenal-crisis, diabetic-ketoacidosis or severe neurological features

administration.cycle_and_sequence: Every 21 days: pembrolizumab first, then paclitaxel and carboplatin for cycles 1–4; pembrolizumab continues as maintenance.
route_and_duration: Pembrolizumab 200 mg intravenously over 30 minutes.
Paclitaxel 200 mg/m² intravenously over 3 hours using non-PVC equipment and an in-line filter.
Carboplatin AUC6 intravenously over approximately 30 minutes, with the protocol dose cap.
practical_workflow: Confirm whether the patient is in induction or maintenance.
During induction, verify paclitaxel premedication, GFR method and current cytotoxic dose levels.
Assess immune and cytotoxic domains separately and use the official protocol for component-specific holds.
observation_and_access: Follow local observation procedures for pembrolizumab and paclitaxel hypersensitivity.
Maintain urgent access for severe immune toxicity, infection or infusion reaction.

regimen_profiles.regimen_role: Trop-2-directed antibody–drug conjugate for previously treated metastatic TNBC
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Sacituzumab govitecan is a Trop-2-directed antibody–drug conjugate carrying SN-38. NCCP 00794 uses it as monotherapy for adults with unresectable or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer after at least two prior systemic therapies, including at least one for advanced disease.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Previously treated unresectable or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: The antibody targets Trop-2 and delivers SN-38, a topoisomerase-I inhibitor, to tumour cells. Intracellular and local payload release causes replication-associated DNA damage, creating both targeted delivery and potential bystander activity.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Sacituzumab govitecan 10 mg/kg intravenously on days 1 and 8 of a 21-day cycle until progression or unacceptable toxicity.
key_points: Antibody–drug conjugate with SN-38 payload
Days 1 and 8 every 21 days
High emetogenic risk
Neutropenia, diarrhoea and infusion reactions are central

patient_selection.treatment_intent: Disease-control and survival-prolonging treatment after prior systemic therapy.
disease_and_biomarker_context: Confirm histologically documented triple-negative disease and the required prior systemic-therapy history.
ASCENT provides direct evidence in heavily pretreated metastatic TNBC; its primary efficacy population excluded patients with brain metastases.
eligibility_orientation: ECOG 0–1 and adequate haematological, renal and liver function in the current protocol.
Review active infection, prior severe neutropenia/diarrhoea and capacity to attend day-1/day-8 treatment.
Address pregnancy/breastfeeding and hypersensitivity exclusions.
important_cautions: UGT1A1*28 homozygosity may increase SN-38 exposure and toxicity; the protocol advises considering a lower starting dose with possible escalation according to cycle-1 tolerance.
Dose reductions for adverse reactions should not be re-escalated.

supportive_care.emetogenic_risk: High under the current NCCP antiemetic classification.
premedication_and_prophylaxis: Use the linked high-risk antiemetic pathway.
Give protocol-directed antipyretic, H1/H2 blockade and corticosteroid premedication as applicable for infusion-reaction prevention.
Use G-CSF according to the protocol’s severe-neutropenia occurrence pathway and local policy.
Provide immediate-access antidiarrhoeal therapy and hydration instructions.
patient_education: Report fever, diarrhoea, vomiting or reduced oral intake early.
Report flushing, rash, wheeze, swelling, dizziness or other infusion symptoms immediately.
Explain day-1/day-8 scheduling and the need for blood-count recovery before treatment.
special_support: Monitor and replace electrolytes when gastrointestinal losses occur.
Consider UGT1A1-related risk when toxicity is disproportionate or known genotype information is available.

baseline: Glucose, electrolytes, magnesium, calcium and phosphate.
ECG and pregnancy testing when clinically indicated.
Baseline diarrhoea, infection and treatment-fitness review.
before_each_cycle: FBC, renal and liver profile before treatment.
Glucose/electrolytes and mineral profile at the protocol-defined interval.
Neutropenia/febrile-neutropenia occurrence count, diarrhoea grade and infusion-reaction history.
Confirm current dose level; do not re-escalate after toxicity reduction.
urgent_review_signals: Fever, rigors or suspected neutropenic sepsis
Persistent diarrhoea, dehydration or inability to maintain intake
Acute infusion reaction, bronchospasm or hypotension
Severe abdominal symptoms or rapid clinical deterioration
Clinically significant electrolyte disturbance or arrhythmia symptoms

administration.cycle_and_sequence: Days 1 and 8 of each 21-day cycle at 10 mg/kg, continued until progression or unacceptable toxicity.
route_and_duration: Intravenous infusion; the initial dose is delivered over 3 hours.
Observe during every infusion and for at least 30 minutes afterwards; later infusion duration follows the official protocol and tolerance.
practical_workflow: Confirm day number, weight-based dose, FBC, diarrhoea status, infection status and current dose level.
Complete antiemetic and infusion-reaction premedication before release.
Keep resuscitation treatment immediately available and use the protocol occurrence-based neutropenia/diarrhoea reductions.
observation_and_access: Continuous clinical observation during infusion and at least 30 minutes post-infusion.
Ensure rapid access for delayed fever, diarrhoea or hypersensitivity symptoms.

regimen_profiles.regimen_role: First-line chemo-immunotherapy for advanced biliary tract cancer
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Durvalumab plus gemcitabine and cisplatin combines PD-L1 blockade with a platinum–antimetabolite backbone for first-line unresectable or metastatic biliary tract cancer, followed by durvalumab maintenance.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: First-line unresectable or metastatic biliary tract cancer
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Durvalumab blocks PD-L1-mediated immune inhibition. Cisplatin produces DNA cross-links, while gemcitabine is incorporated into DNA and inhibits nucleotide synthesis. Cytotoxic tumour injury and immune checkpoint blockade provide complementary activity.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Cycles 1–8 are 21 days: durvalumab on day 1 and gemcitabine/cisplatin on days 1 and 8. From cycle 9, durvalumab continues every 28 days until progression or unacceptable toxicity.
key_points: Induction chemotherapy plus durvalumab followed by maintenance
Day-1/day-8 cisplatin and gemcitabine
Cisplatin hydration, electrolyte and renal safeguards
Biliary infection and immune toxicity require separate assessment

patient_selection.treatment_intent: Disease-control and survival-prolonging first-line systemic therapy.
disease_and_biomarker_context: Confirm unresectable or metastatic biliary tract cancer and no prior systemic therapy for advanced disease.
The official PDF lists PD-L1 testing among baseline tests; interpretation and reimbursement relevance should follow the current national pathway.
The TOPAZ-1 evidence record maps directly to the treatment strategy.
eligibility_orientation: ECOG 0–2 and adequate haematological, hepatic and renal function in the current protocol.
Assess cisplatin suitability, creatinine clearance, hearing and neuropathy.
Review autoimmune disease, immunosuppression, infection, biliary stents/drains and prior severe immune toxicity.
important_cautions: Patients with biliary obstruction or stents may be at increased risk of cholangitis; fever and cholestatic deterioration need urgent source assessment, not automatic attribution to immune toxicity.
The current official PDF is version 3 but its stated review date has passed; verify the live NCCP listing before relying on version status.

supportive_care.emetogenic_risk: High because the regimen contains cisplatin; use the current high-risk antiemetic pathway.
premedication_and_prophylaxis: Provide protocol-directed pre/post hydration and magnesium with potassium when indicated for cisplatin.
Use the linked high-risk antiemetic pathway.
Provide immune-toxicity education and a direct contact pathway.
patient_education: Report fever, rigors, right-upper-quadrant pain, jaundice or changes in biliary drainage urgently.
Report reduced urine output, hearing change, tinnitus, neuropathy or severe vomiting.
Report new cough, breathlessness, diarrhoea, rash, endocrine symptoms or marked fatigue.
special_support: Coordinate biliary drainage/stent management and infection plans with hepatobiliary teams.
Review fluid tolerance and electrolyte replacement in patients with cardiovascular or renal comorbidity.

baseline: FBC, renal and liver profile, glucose and thyroid function.
Hepatitis B/C screening and PD-L1 testing as listed by the official protocol.
Audiology and creatinine clearance when clinically indicated.
before_each_cycle: Day 1: FBC, renal and liver profile, glucose and immune-toxicity screening.
Day 8: FBC and creatinine/renal review before gemcitabine/cisplatin.
Thyroid function at the protocol-defined interval.
Assess cholangitis, obstruction, hydration, electrolyte, hearing and neuropathy symptoms.
priority_toxicities: Cisplatin nephrotoxicity, electrolyte loss, ototoxicity and neuropathy
Immune pneumonitis, colitis, hepatitis, endocrine and other organ toxicities
urgent_review_signals: Fever/rigors with biliary stent, jaundice or abdominal pain
Oliguria, significant creatinine rise or severe electrolyte disturbance
New hearing loss or disabling neuropathy
New hypoxia, chest pain or serious immune-toxicity features
Severe cytopenia, bleeding or suspected sepsis

administration.cycle_and_sequence: Cycles 1–8: durvalumab on day 1, then gemcitabine and cisplatin on days 1 and 8 of a 21-day cycle; cycle 9 onward: durvalumab every 28 days.
route_and_duration: Durvalumab is infused intravenously over 60 minutes.
Gemcitabine and cisplatin are administered intravenously with protocol-directed cisplatin hydration and electrolyte support.
practical_workflow: Confirm induction versus maintenance phase and day 1 versus day 8.
Before cisplatin, verify renal function, hydration suitability, electrolytes and urine output according to local policy.
Assess infection/biliary and immune-toxicity mechanisms separately before withholding or treating.
observation_and_access: Follow local infusion-reaction procedures for durvalumab and cytotoxic therapy.
Maintain urgent access for cholangitis/sepsis, renal deterioration or severe immune toxicity.

regimen_profiles.regimen_role: Oral fluoropyrimidine and oxaliplatin backbone across colorectal and gastric indications
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: XELOX/CAPOX combines oral capecitabine with day-1 oxaliplatin. The shared NCCP protocol covers adjuvant stage III colon cancer, advanced or metastatic colorectal cancer, and adjuvant stage II/III gastric adenocarcinoma after D2 gastrectomy. The selected disease context determines intent, duration and the most applicable evidence.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Adjuvant stage III colon cancer; advanced/metastatic colorectal cancer; adjuvant stage II/III gastric adenocarcinoma after D2 gastrectomy
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Capecitabine is converted to fluorouracil and produces sustained fluoropyrimidine antimetabolite activity. Oxaliplatin forms platinum–DNA adducts. Their non-overlapping mechanisms provide systemic cytotoxic activity while the oral fluoropyrimidine avoids a continuous-infusion pump.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Every 21 days: oxaliplatin 130 mg/m² intravenously on day 1 and capecitabine 1000 mg/m² twice daily on days 1–14, followed by a 7-day rest. The NCCP protocol permits 3 or 6 months in adjuvant colon cancer at consultant discretion and treatment until progression or unacceptable toxicity in metastatic disease.
key_points: Three distinct NCCP indications
Oral adherence and toxicity interruption plan are essential
DPD status before capecitabine
Oxaliplatin neuropathy and cold sensitivity
Renal function directly affects capecitabine safety

patient_selection.treatment_intent: Potentially curative adjuvant treatment in resected colon or gastric cancer, or disease-control treatment in advanced/metastatic colorectal cancer.
disease_and_biomarker_context: Confirm which of the three NCCP indications is being treated before interpreting duration or evidence.
Confirm DPD testing before first capecitabine exposure unless already appropriately documented.
For gastric cancer, confirm the postoperative D2-gastrectomy setting specified by the protocol.
eligibility_orientation: Review ECOG status, blood counts, renal and hepatic function.
Assess baseline peripheral neuropathy and cardiovascular comorbidity.
Confirm the patient can understand and safely self-administer an oral twice-daily schedule.
important_cautions: Severe renal impairment, severe hepatic impairment, complete DPD deficiency and functionally significant baseline neuropathy are protocol exclusions.
IDEA duration data require disease-risk and regimen-specific interpretation; they are not a universal three-month rule.

supportive_care.emetogenic_risk: Moderate overall, driven mainly by oxaliplatin; use the current protocol-linked antiemetic pathway.
premedication_and_prophylaxis: Provide protocol-concordant antiemetics before oxaliplatin and a breakthrough plan.
Complete fluoropyrimidine/DPD counselling before first treatment.
patient_education: Take capecitabine with food or within 30 minutes after food and do not replace omitted doses.
Stop capecitabine and contact the team promptly for moderate or severe diarrhoea, stomatitis, hand–foot syndrome, fever, chest pain or dehydration.
Avoid cold drinks, cold air and direct cold exposure around oxaliplatin because acute dysaesthesia may be triggered.
special_support: Use a written oral treatment calendar and medication-reconciliation check.
Review anticoagulant interactions, especially warfarin, and assess adherence at each cycle.

baseline: DPD phenotype and/or genotype testing before capecitabine.
before_each_cycle: FBC, renal and liver profile.
Actual capecitabine doses taken, interruptions and missed doses.
Current and worst diarrhoea, stomatitis and hand–foot syndrome.
Peripheral-neuropathy grade, persistence and functional effect.
priority_toxicities: Capecitabine diarrhoea, stomatitis and hand–foot syndrome
Oxaliplatin sensory neuropathy and laryngopharyngeal dysaesthesia
urgent_review_signals: Chest pain or acute cardiac symptoms
Severe diarrhoea, dehydration or inability to maintain oral intake
New functional neuropathy or persistent laryngopharyngeal symptoms

administration.cycle_and_sequence: Oxaliplatin on day 1, followed by capecitabine twice daily on days 1–14 of a 21-day cycle.
route_and_duration: Oxaliplatin is infused intravenously in glucose 5%; sodium chloride is incompatible.
Capecitabine is taken orally with food on days 1–14.
practical_workflow: Confirm indication, intended duration and current dose level before prescribing.
Dispense the exact tablet combination with a written calendar and interruption instructions.
Use the official NCCP tables for blood-count, renal, hepatic, gastrointestinal, hand–foot and neuropathy modifications.
observation_and_access: Facilities for anaphylaxis treatment must be available during oxaliplatin administration.
Longer infusion may be considered according to the protocol after laryngopharyngeal dysaesthesia.

indications_reviewed: Adjuvant stage III colon cancer
Advanced/metastatic colorectal cancer
Adjuvant stage II/III gastric cancer after D2 gastrectomy
evidence_audit.coverage_summary: NO16968 supports adjuvant stage III colon cancer, NO16966 supports metastatic colorectal cancer, CLASSIC supports post-D2 gastric cancer, and IDEA provides duration context.
evidence_audit.later_or_add_on_search: No later add-on trial was used to create an unencoded combination pathway. Duration evidence was included because it directly affects the 3-versus-6-month protocol context.
remaining_uncertainties: IDEA duration choice remains risk- and regimen-dependent.
Trial populations do not reproduce every local eligibility or dose-modification rule.

regimen_profiles.regimen_role: Weekly single-agent taxane across four later-line solid-tumour indications
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Weekly paclitaxel 80 mg/m² is an NCCP shared protocol for metastatic breast cancer, second-line metastatic ovarian cancer, relapsed/refractory small-cell lung cancer and second-line metastatic bladder cancer. The evidence strength is not uniform: randomized phase 3 evidence exists for the weekly schedule in metastatic breast cancer, while the ovarian, SCLC and bladder indications are supported primarily by smaller phase 2 or retrospective studies.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Metastatic breast; second-line metastatic ovarian; relapsed/refractory SCLC; second-line metastatic bladder cancer
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Paclitaxel stabilises microtubules and prevents normal mitotic spindle disassembly, leading to cell-cycle arrest and cell death. Weekly exposure alters dose intensity and toxicity compared with three-weekly administration.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Paclitaxel 80 mg/m² intravenously on days 1, 8, 15 and 22 of a 28-day cycle until progression or unacceptable toxicity; days 1, 8 and 15 may be used at consultant discretion.
key_points: Four-indication shared protocol
Weekly blood-count and neuropathy surveillance
Low emetogenic risk
Hypersensitivity premedication pathway
Evidence quality varies substantially by indication

patient_selection.treatment_intent: Palliative disease-control treatment after the indication-specific prior therapy described by the NCCP protocol.
disease_and_biomarker_context: Confirm the exact tumour type and prior treatment line before assessment.
The ovarian, SCLC and bladder indications are outside the licensed indication in Ireland according to the NCCP protocol and require local unlicensed-use consent processes.
eligibility_orientation: ECOG 0–2 and adequate blood counts, renal and hepatic assessment.
Review baseline neuropathy and previous taxane exposure.
Assess prior paclitaxel hypersensitivity and whether a nab-paclitaxel switch pathway is relevant.
important_cautions: The efficacy evidence is strongest for metastatic breast cancer and materially weaker for the other three indications.
A single shared regimen card must not imply equal certainty across tumour types.

supportive_care.emetogenic_risk: Low according to the current NCCP classification; use the current NCCP Medical Oncology antiemetic guidance.
premedication_and_prophylaxis: Initial treatment requires corticosteroid, antihistamine and H2-antagonist premedication according to the protocol.
The protocol permits de-escalation of dexamethasone and potentially famotidine after tolerance, subject to consultant guidance and local policy.
patient_education: Report fever, rash, dyspnoea or infusion symptoms immediately.
Report numbness, pain, weakness, balance difficulty or loss of fine motor function before the next dose.
Myalgia and arthralgia may occur; provide an agreed analgesia plan.
special_support: Consider scalp-cooling availability where appropriate.
Document hypersensitivity history and any premedication de-escalation decision.

baseline: Prior taxane exposure and hypersensitivity history.
before_each_cycle: FBC, renal and liver profile before treatment; day-8 FBC as specified.
Peripheral-neuropathy grade and functional effect.
Any hypersensitivity, myalgia/arthralgia or non-haematological toxicity since the last dose.
urgent_review_signals: Infusion reaction, bronchospasm, hypotension or angioedema
New motor weakness or grade 2 or greater neuropathy

administration.cycle_and_sequence: Paclitaxel is given weekly on days 1, 8, 15 and 22 of a 28-day cycle, with a days 1, 8 and 15 option at consultant discretion.
route_and_duration: Intravenous infusion over 60 minutes.
Use non-PVC containers and giving sets with the specified in-line filter.
practical_workflow: Confirm tumour indication and treatment line because the same protocol spans four cancers.
Verify premedication plan and whether dexamethasone/famotidine de-escalation has been authorised.
Use the protocol’s haematological, hepatic and neuropathy tables for each weekly decision.
observation_and_access: Facilities to manage anaphylaxis must be present.
Observe closely during early doses and after any previous hypersensitivity reaction.

evidence_audit.status: Complete with explicit evidence-strength gradient
indications_reviewed: Metastatic breast cancer
Platinum-resistant/refractory ovarian cancer
Relapsed/refractory SCLC
Post-cisplatin metastatic urothelial bladder cancer
evidence_audit.coverage_summary: CALGB 9840 provides randomized weekly-versus-three-weekly breast evidence. The ovarian and SCLC indications are supported by phase 2 studies; the bladder indication is supported by a small retrospective cohort and earlier phase 2 experience.
evidence_audit.later_or_add_on_search: No contemporary combination evidence was allowed to imply that the single-agent weekly protocol includes additional medicines.
remaining_uncertainties: No phase 3 randomized validation was identified for the exact weekly single-agent schedule in the ovarian, SCLC or bladder indications.
Modern treatment sequencing may differ from the populations in the older studies.

regimen_profiles.regimen_role: HER2-directed antibody–drug conjugate for HER2-positive and HER2-low metastatic breast cancer
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Trastuzumab deruxtecan is a HER2-targeted antibody–drug conjugate used as monotherapy in two NCCP-defined populations: previously treated HER2-positive unresectable/metastatic breast cancer and HER2-low unresectable/metastatic breast cancer after chemotherapy in the metastatic setting or early recurrence after adjuvant chemotherapy.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Unresectable or metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer after prior anti-HER2 therapy; or HER2-low breast cancer after prior chemotherapy in the NCCP-defined setting
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: The HER2-directed antibody delivers a cleavable topoisomerase-I inhibitor payload into HER2-expressing tumour cells. The membrane-permeable payload can also affect nearby tumour cells, which is mechanistically relevant to HER2-low heterogeneous disease.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Trastuzumab deruxtecan 5.4 mg/kg intravenously on day 1 of a 21-day cycle until progression or unacceptable toxicity. The first infusion is over 90 minutes and subsequent tolerated infusions may be shortened to 30 minutes.
key_points: Two biomarker-defined indications
HER2 status must match the exact NCCP definition
Interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis is a critical safety risk
High emetogenic potential
LVEF monitoring every 12 weeks

patient_selection.treatment_intent: Palliative disease-control treatment intended to prolong progression-free and overall survival in the relevant metastatic HER2-defined population.
disease_and_biomarker_context: HER2-positive: IHC 3+ or amplified by validated ISH/FISH methodology as defined by the protocol.
HER2-low: IHC 1+ or IHC 2+/ISH-negative by a validated assay.
Confirm the prior anti-HER2 or chemotherapy exposure and recurrence timing required for the selected indication.
eligibility_orientation: Adult patient with ECOG 0–2.
LVEF at least 50% and adequate blood counts, renal and liver function.
Review CNS disease status and respiratory history.
important_cautions: History of ILD or pneumonitis is an exclusion in the current protocol.
Untreated or symptomatic CNS metastases and significant cardiac disease require specific caution/exclusion review.

supportive_care.emetogenic_risk: High; use the current NCCP high-risk antiemetic pathway and reassess delayed nausea at every cycle.
premedication_and_prophylaxis: Administer high-risk antiemetic prophylaxis before each cycle.
No routine corticosteroid premedication should obscure early respiratory symptom assessment unless required by the antiemetic pathway.
patient_education: Report new cough, dyspnoea, fever or reduced exercise tolerance immediately; do not wait for the next cycle.
Explain that treatment may be interrupted while ILD/pneumonitis is investigated.
Provide a clear plan for delayed nausea, vomiting, constipation and hydration.
special_support: Low threshold for respiratory assessment and thoracic imaging when ILD is suspected.
Coordinate cardiac monitoring and pregnancy-prevention counselling.

baseline: ECHO or MUGA confirming LVEF at least 50%.
Respiratory history, baseline symptoms and prior ILD/pneumonitis review.
before_each_cycle: FBC, renal and liver profile.
Directed cough, dyspnoea, fever and exercise-tolerance screen.
Nausea/vomiting control, fatigue and infusion-related symptoms.
LVEF every 12 weeks, or more frequently if cardiac impairment is suspected.
urgent_review_signals: Any new respiratory symptom or unexplained hypoxia
Symptomatic heart failure or significant LVEF decline

administration.cycle_and_sequence: Day 1 every 21 days until progression or unacceptable toxicity.
route_and_duration: Intravenous infusion in glucose 5%.
First infusion over 90 minutes; subsequent well-tolerated doses may be given over 30 minutes.
Use the specified 0.20 or 0.22 micron in-line PES or PS filter; do not administer as a push or bolus.
practical_workflow: Confirm exact HER2 category and prior-treatment criterion before prescribing.
Complete respiratory symptom screen immediately before each dose.
Use the official NCCP ILD, haematological, cardiac and organ-function dose-modification tables.
observation_and_access: Slow or interrupt infusion for infusion-related symptoms.
Permanently discontinue for severe infusion reactions and follow the protocol for ILD grade-specific action.

evidence_audit.status: Complete for both encoded biomarker-defined indications
indications_reviewed: Previously treated HER2-positive unresectable/metastatic breast cancer
Previously treated HER2-low unresectable/metastatic breast cancer
evidence_audit.coverage_summary: DESTINY-Breast03 supports the HER2-positive post-trastuzumab/taxane setting and DESTINY-Breast04 supports the HER2-low post-chemotherapy setting. Mature DESTINY-Breast03 survival follow-up is linked.
evidence_audit.later_or_add_on_search: Later T-DXd studies in earlier lines and HER2-ultralow disease were reviewed as contextual landscape changes but were not used to expand the two encoded NCCP indications.
remaining_uncertainties: Trial HER2 testing and central-review processes may not fully reproduce routine pathology practice.
The protocol’s ILD safeguards remain operationally more important than efficacy evidence when assessing acute respiratory symptoms.

regimen_profiles.regimen_role: First line antibody drug conjugate plus PD 1 checkpoint inhibition
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab is used by the current NCCP protocol for first line treatment of unresectable or metastatic urothelial cancer in adults who are eligible for platinum containing chemotherapy. The regimen combines Nectin 4 directed payload delivery with PD 1 checkpoint inhibition and has phase 3 survival evidence from EV 302.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: First line unresectable or metastatic urothelial carcinoma in the current NCCP defined population
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Enfortumab vedotin targets Nectin 4 and delivers the microtubule disrupting payload monomethyl auristatin E. Pembrolizumab blocks PD 1 signalling. The combination therefore couples targeted cytotoxic delivery with immune checkpoint inhibition.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: The standard NCCP schedule is enfortumab vedotin 1.25 mg/kg on days 1 and 8 with pembrolizumab 200 mg on day 1 of a 21 day cycle. The NCCP protocol also provides a 42 day option using enfortumab vedotin on days 1, 8, 22 and 29 with pembrolizumab 400 mg on day 1. Treatment continues until progression or unacceptable toxicity.
key_points: First line advanced urothelial cancer
Two NCCP schedule options
Skin toxicity, neuropathy and hyperglycaemia require active surveillance
Immune related toxicity remains independently relevant
EV 302 includes mature follow up beyond the primary analysis

patient_selection.treatment_intent: Palliative systemic treatment intended to improve disease control and survival in unresectable or metastatic urothelial carcinoma.
disease_and_biomarker_context: Confirm urothelial carcinoma and the exact current NCCP indication.
The current NCCP protocol specifies adults who are eligible for platinum containing chemotherapy.
No PD L1 selection criterion is required by the current NCCP regimen.
eligibility_orientation: ECOG 0 to 2 and adequate haematological and organ function.
Review baseline glucose control, neuropathy, skin status and ocular history.
Confirm that infection, CNS disease and immunosuppression do not create an NCCP caution or exclusion.
important_cautions: Uncontrolled diabetes mellitus.
Pre existing grade greater than 2 sensory or motor neuropathy.
Active keratitis or corneal ulceration.
History of interstitial lung disease, clinically significant infection or active CNS metastases requires specific review.

supportive_care.emetogenic_risk: Low according to the current NCCP parenteral SACT classification because enfortumab vedotin is classified as low risk while pembrolizumab is minimal risk. Use the current NCCP Medical Oncology antiemetic guidance.
premedication_and_prophylaxis: Use NCCP antiemetic guidance appropriate to low emetogenic risk and individual prior nausea history.
Do not use routine immunosuppression that could obscure immune related toxicity unless clinically required.
patient_education: Report new blistering, painful rash, mucosal symptoms or rapidly progressive skin change urgently.
Report worsening numbness, weakness, gait change or fine motor impairment.
Report marked thirst, polyuria, confusion or other symptoms of hyperglycaemia.
Report cough, dyspnoea, diarrhoea, jaundice, endocrine symptoms or other possible immune toxicity promptly.
special_support: Provide proactive skin care advice and frequent skin review.
Ensure diabetes management support when glucose control deteriorates.
Arrange ophthalmology review when ocular symptoms or corneal toxicity are suspected.

baseline: Lipase, phosphate, blood glucose and HbA1c.
Skin assessment and ophthalmology assessment when clinically indicated.
Thyroid function tests and ECG when clinically indicated.
before_each_cycle: FBC, renal and liver profile and blood glucose on day 1 and day 8 of cycle 1, then day 1 of subsequent cycles as specified by NCCP.
Phosphate prior to each cycle.
Lipase, HbA1c and additional glucose testing as clinically indicated.
Ongoing skin and neuropathy assessment.
Thyroid function every 3 to 6 weeks and cortisol when clinically indicated.
priority_toxicities: Immune related pneumonitis, colitis, hepatitis, nephritis and endocrinopathy
urgent_review_signals: Blistering or exfoliative rash, mucosal involvement or rapidly worsening skin toxicity
New significant motor or sensory neuropathy
New respiratory symptoms or unexplained hypoxia
Severe diarrhoea, hepatitis, neurological or endocrine symptoms

administration.cycle_and_sequence: On the 21 day schedule, enfortumab vedotin is administered first on days 1 and 8 and pembrolizumab is administered on day 1. The NCCP protocol also provides a 42 day schedule.
route_and_duration: Enfortumab vedotin is given by intravenous infusion over 30 minutes.
Pembrolizumab is given by intravenous infusion over 30 minutes.
practical_workflow: Confirm weight because enfortumab vedotin has a maximum dose for patients over 100 kg.
Check skin, glucose and neuropathy before treatment.
Use component specific dose modification pathways. Pembrolizumab dose reduction is not recommended.
observation_and_access: Facilities to manage anaphylaxis must be available.
Use the filtration and dilution instructions specified in the current NCCP protocol.

evidence_audit.status: Complete with mature EV 302 follow up included
indications_reviewed: First line unresectable or metastatic urothelial carcinoma
evidence_audit.coverage_summary: EV 302 provides phase 3 evidence for enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab versus platinum based chemotherapy. The 2.5 year analysis confirms sustained progression free and overall survival benefit.
evidence_audit.later_or_add_on_search: Primary EV 302 results, mature follow up and prespecified subgroup analyses were checked. No separate add on strategy was allowed to generate an unencoded SACTCheck regimen.
remaining_uncertainties: The current NCCP indication wording and treatment details remain the operational source.
Independent consultant oncology and oncology pharmacy review remains pending.

regimen_profiles.regimen_role: First line nivolumab plus fluoropyrimidine and oxaliplatin chemotherapy for selected advanced upper gastrointestinal cancers
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Nivolumab plus modified FOLFOX6 is used by NCCP in two distinct first line contexts. One is unresectable advanced, recurrent or metastatic oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma with tumour cell PD L1 expression at least 1 percent. The other is HER2 negative advanced or metastatic gastric, gastroesophageal junction or oesophageal adenocarcinoma with PD L1 CPS at least 5. The evidence base is therefore indication specific and must not be represented by one trial alone.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: First line advanced oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma with the required PD L1 expression, or HER2 negative advanced gastric, gastroesophageal junction or oesophageal adenocarcinoma with PD L1 CPS at least 5
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Nivolumab blocks PD 1 signalling. Oxaliplatin produces platinum DNA damage, while fluorouracil inhibits thymidylate synthase and is potentiated by folinic acid. The regimen combines checkpoint inhibition with an established fluoropyrimidine and platinum backbone.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Nivolumab and modified FOLFOX6 are given on day 1 of a 14 day cycle. Nivolumab may be given using the current NCCP intravenous or subcutaneous presentation and is continued for up to 24 months or until progression or unacceptable toxicity. Modified FOLFOX6 continues until progression or unacceptable toxicity.
key_points: Two separate tumour and biomarker indications
CheckMate 649 supports the adenocarcinoma context
CheckMate 648 supports the oesophageal squamous context
Moderate emetogenic risk is driven by oxaliplatin
DPD testing is required before first fluorouracil exposure unless previously completed

patient_selection.treatment_intent: Palliative first line systemic treatment intended to improve disease control and survival in the appropriate advanced upper gastrointestinal cancer population.
disease_and_biomarker_context: OSCC requires tumour cell PD L1 expression at least 1 percent by a validated method.
Gastric, gastroesophageal junction and oesophageal adenocarcinoma requires HER2 negative disease and PD L1 CPS at least 5.
Confirm the exact histology and biomarker context before selecting evidence or applying the protocol.
eligibility_orientation: ECOG 0 to 2 with adequate haematological, hepatic and renal function.
Complete DPD assessment before first fluorouracil treatment unless already tested.
Review baseline neuropathy, autoimmune history, infection, CNS disease and cardiac risk.
important_cautions: Clinically significant autoimmune disease or immunosuppression.
Active clinically significant infection.
Symptomatic peripheral neuropathy.
Recent myocardial infarction, uncontrolled angina, hypertension, arrhythmia or heart failure.
Known DPD deficiency and functional baseline neuropathy are exclusions in the current protocol.

supportive_care.emetogenic_risk: Moderate according to the current NCCP parenteral SACT classification because oxaliplatin is classified as moderate risk. Use the current NCCP Medical Oncology antiemetic guidance.
premedication_and_prophylaxis: Use NCCP moderate risk antiemetic guidance and individualise for prior nausea and vomiting.
Avoid oral cryotherapy with ice during the fluorouracil bolus in this oxaliplatin regimen because cold exposure can precipitate acute oxaliplatin neurotoxicity.
patient_education: Avoid cold exposure around oxaliplatin and report throat tightness, dysaesthesia or breathing difficulty immediately.
Report diarrhoea, stomatitis, fever, neuropathy or significant hand foot symptoms before treatment.
Report cough, dyspnoea, endocrine symptoms, jaundice or other possible immune toxicity promptly.
special_support: Provide DPD counselling where partial deficiency is identified.
Ensure ambulatory infusion pump and venous access arrangements for the 46 hour fluorouracil infusion.

baseline: FBC, renal and liver profile, blood glucose and thyroid function.
DPD testing before first fluorouracil exposure unless previously completed.
PD L1 testing for the intended nivolumab indication.
HER2 testing for the gastric, gastroesophageal junction or oesophageal adenocarcinoma indication.
ECG if cardiac function is compromised.
before_each_cycle: FBC, renal and liver profile and glucose.
Thyroid function before each cycle and cortisol when clinically indicated.
Peripheral neuropathy review at least every two cycles.
Review diarrhoea, stomatitis, infection and immune related symptoms.
priority_toxicities: Renal and hepatic impairment affecting chemotherapy components
Immune related pneumonitis, colitis, hepatitis, nephritis and endocrinopathy
urgent_review_signals: Progressive motor or function limiting neuropathy
Severe mucositis or early severe fluoropyrimidine toxicity
Cardiac chest pain or acute cardiac symptoms during fluoropyrimidine treatment

administration.cycle_and_sequence: Nivolumab is administered before the modified FOLFOX6 components. Oxaliplatin precedes fluorouracil and may run with folinic acid using the protocol specified connector. Folinic acid is given before fluorouracil.
route_and_duration: Nivolumab uses the current NCCP intravenous or subcutaneous schedule.
Oxaliplatin and folinic acid are infused over 2 hours.
Fluorouracil includes a bolus followed by a 46 hour continuous intravenous infusion.
practical_workflow: Do not use sodium chloride 0.9 percent to piggyback or flush oxaliplatin.
Increase oxaliplatin infusion duration when required for laryngopharyngeal dysaesthesia.
Confirm pump arrangements before the continuous fluorouracil infusion.
observation_and_access: Facilities to manage anaphylaxis must be present.
Assess both infusion reactions and delayed immune related toxicity across the full treatment course.

evidence_audit.status: Complete across both encoded indications with mature follow up
indications_reviewed: Advanced oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma with tumour cell PD L1 at least 1 percent
HER2 negative advanced gastric, gastroesophageal junction or oesophageal adenocarcinoma with PD L1 CPS at least 5
evidence_audit.coverage_summary: CheckMate 649 supports nivolumab with fluoropyrimidine and oxaliplatin chemotherapy for gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma. CheckMate 648 independently supports nivolumab plus fluoropyrimidine and platinum chemotherapy for advanced oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma.
evidence_audit.later_or_add_on_search: Primary publications and mature follow up were checked for both CheckMate 649 and CheckMate 648. Five year CheckMate 649 follow up and the 29 month CheckMate 648 analysis are linked as subsequent evidence.
remaining_uncertainties: CheckMate 648 used cisplatin plus fluorouracil rather than the exact modified FOLFOX6 backbone, so its mapping to the NCCP oxaliplatin regimen is evidence for the nivolumab plus fluoropyrimidine and platinum strategy rather than an exact schedule match.
The current NCCP biomarker criteria and schedule remain authoritative.
