regimen_profiles.regimen_role: Dual checkpoint inhibition followed by nivolumab maintenance for advanced melanoma
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Nivolumab plus ipilimumab is an immune checkpoint combination for adults with advanced unresectable or metastatic melanoma. The current NCCP regimen gives four combination cycles followed by nivolumab monotherapy. CheckMate 067 provides long term randomised evidence and final 10 year outcomes, while CheckMate 204 provides important contextual evidence for selected patients with melanoma brain metastases.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Advanced unresectable or metastatic melanoma in adults
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Nivolumab blocks PD 1 signalling in activated T cells. Ipilimumab blocks CTLA 4 mediated inhibition during T cell priming. Combined blockade acts at complementary immune checkpoints and increases antitumour activity, but also increases the frequency and complexity of immune related toxicity.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Cycles 1 to 4 use nivolumab 1 mg/kg plus ipilimumab 3 mg/kg every 21 days. From cycle 5, nivolumab continues as monotherapy using the current NCCP intravenous or subcutaneous schedule until progression or unacceptable toxicity.
key_points: Advanced melanoma
Four combination cycles then nivolumab maintenance
Final 10 year CheckMate 067 survival data included
Brain metastasis evidence is contextual and does not override NCCP CNS cautions
Immune related toxicity surveillance is central

patient_selection.treatment_intent: Palliative systemic immunotherapy intended to achieve durable disease control and prolong survival in advanced melanoma.
disease_and_biomarker_context: Adult with unresectable or metastatic melanoma.
BRAF status should be available because it informs the wider treatment strategy even though it is not a selection requirement for this combination.
PD L1 expression is not required by the current NCCP indication.
eligibility_orientation: ECOG 0 to 1 with adequate haematological, hepatic and renal function.
Review autoimmune disease, infection, corticosteroid or immunosuppressive use and CNS symptoms.
Assess pregnancy and contraception requirements.
important_cautions: Clinically significant autoimmune disease.
Immunosuppressive doses of systemic corticosteroids or other immunosuppression.
Active clinically significant infection.
Symptomatic CNS metastases are a caution in the current NCCP protocol.
Symptomatic interstitial lung disease is an exclusion.

supportive_care.emetogenic_risk: Low according to the current NCCP parenteral SACT classification because ipilimumab is classified as low risk while nivolumab is minimal risk. Use the current NCCP Medical Oncology antiemetic guidance.
premedication_and_prophylaxis: Routine antiemetic prophylaxis should follow current NCCP low risk guidance and individual prior nausea history.
When high dose corticosteroids are required for immune toxicity, follow the protocol taper and infection prevention considerations.
patient_education: Provide explicit education on diarrhoea, rash, cough, dyspnoea, jaundice, headache, visual change, weakness and endocrine symptoms.
Explain that immune toxicity can occur during treatment or after the last dose.
Provide clear urgent contact instructions because early immune toxicity assessment can alter management.
special_support: Low threshold for endocrine, respiratory, neurological and cardiac investigation when symptoms emerge.
Document the plan for steroid taper and opportunistic infection prophylaxis when prolonged immunosuppression is required.

baseline: Blood glucose and thyroid function tests.
Clinical review for autoimmune disease, infection, respiratory symptoms and CNS symptoms.
before_each_cycle: FBC, renal and liver profile and blood glucose.
Thyroid function before each cycle and cortisol when clinically indicated.
Directed screen for respiratory, gastrointestinal, hepatic, endocrine, neurological, dermatological and cardiac immune toxicity.
priority_toxicities: Endocrinopathies including hypophysitis and thyroid dysfunction
urgent_review_signals: New dyspnoea, cough or unexplained hypoxia
Severe headache, visual symptoms, profound fatigue or hypotension suggesting endocrine toxicity
Weakness, sensory change, confusion, chest pain, arrhythmia or other possible neurological or cardiac immune toxicity

administration.cycle_and_sequence: For cycles 1 to 4, nivolumab and ipilimumab are given every 21 days. From cycle 5, nivolumab continues alone. If either agent is withheld during the combination phase, the other is also withheld according to the current NCCP protocol.
route_and_duration: Nivolumab 1 mg/kg is infused over 30 minutes during combination treatment.
Ipilimumab 3 mg/kg is infused over 30 minutes.
Maintenance nivolumab may use current NCCP intravenous or subcutaneous formulations.
practical_workflow: Confirm which treatment phase is being assessed because the combination and maintenance phases differ.
Review immune toxicity before every administration and do not reduce checkpoint inhibitor dose as a substitute for protocol directed withholding or discontinuation.
observation_and_access: Facilities to treat anaphylaxis must be present.
During the combination phase, follow the NCCP observation requirements and vital sign monitoring around infusion.

evidence_audit.status: Complete with final 10 year follow up and CNS contextual evidence
indications_reviewed: Advanced unresectable or metastatic melanoma in adults
evidence_audit.coverage_summary: CheckMate 067 provides randomised phase 3 evidence for nivolumab plus ipilimumab and includes final 10 year survival outcomes. CheckMate 204 provides contextual evidence for selected patients with melanoma brain metastases.
evidence_audit.later_or_add_on_search: Foundational CheckMate 067 evidence, final 10 year follow up and prospective CNS specific evidence were checked. Later treatment options were not used to imply that this encoded regimen includes additional medicines.
remaining_uncertainties: CheckMate 067 was not designed for a formal powered comparison of nivolumab plus ipilimumab versus nivolumab alone, so descriptive differences between those two groups should not be overstated.
CheckMate 204 CNS outcomes apply to selected study populations and do not override the current NCCP caution for symptomatic CNS metastases.

regimen_profiles.regimen_role: Every 3 week taxane plus continuous corticosteroid for metastatic castration resistant prostate cancer
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Docetaxel 75 mg/m² plus prednisolone is the current NCCP regimen for hormone refractory metastatic prostate cancer. TAX 327 provides the pivotal randomised survival evidence for every 3 week docetaxel with prednisone and supports the same corticosteroid treatment family represented by the NCCP prednisolone schedule.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Metastatic castration resistant prostate cancer
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Docetaxel stabilises microtubules and disrupts mitosis. Prednisolone is administered continuously as part of the established taxane regimen and provides glucocorticoid activity within the treatment schedule.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Docetaxel 75 mg/m² is given intravenously on day 1 every 21 days. Prednisolone 10 mg daily, or 5 mg twice daily, is continued through the cycle. Treatment continues according to the current NCCP treatment plan until progression, unacceptable toxicity or a consultant directed stopping decision.
key_points: Metastatic castration resistant prostate cancer
Every 3 week docetaxel is the TAX 327 survival supported schedule
Continuous prednisolone forms part of the regimen
Docetaxel steroid premedication is separate from the continuous prednisolone schedule
Modern treatment sequencing should be interpreted separately from the original pivotal trial

patient_selection.treatment_intent: Palliative systemic treatment intended to improve disease control, symptoms and survival in metastatic castration resistant prostate cancer.
disease_and_biomarker_context: Confirm metastatic prostate cancer in the castration resistant or hormone refractory setting represented by NCCP 00546.
Do not use this profile as evidence for docetaxel in hormone sensitive metastatic prostate cancer, which is represented by a separate NCCP regimen.
eligibility_orientation: Confirm the current NCCP indication and consultant treatment plan.
ECOG performance status and adequate marrow and organ function should be assessed against the current source.
Docetaxel should not be administered when the neutrophil count is below the source threshold.
important_cautions: Hepatic dysfunction can increase docetaxel exposure and toxicity.
Previous severe docetaxel hypersensitivity is clinically important.
Peripheral neuropathy, severe skin toxicity and stomatitis can require treatment modification.
CYP3A interacting medicines require review.

supportive_care.emetogenic_risk: Low emetogenic risk in the current SACTCheck mapping. Use the linked national NCCP antiemetic guidance.
premedication_and_prophylaxis: Oral dexamethasone 8 mg at 12 hours, 3 hours and 1 hour before docetaxel is specified by NCCP.
If oral dexamethasone has been missed, the NCCP source permits consideration of dexamethasone 20 mg intravenously immediately before chemotherapy at consultant discretion.
Prophylactic G CSF may be used to mitigate haematological toxicity where clinically appropriate.
patient_education: Report fever or infection symptoms urgently.
Report worsening neuropathy, severe mouth symptoms, skin toxicity or hypersensitivity symptoms.
Explain that continuous prednisolone and docetaxel premedication have different purposes.
special_support: Review corticosteroid adverse effects over repeated cycles.
Assess fluid retention and hypersensitivity risk with docetaxel.

before_each_cycle: FBC
Renal profile
Liver profile
Neuropathy, mucosal and skin toxicity review
Infection assessment

administration.cycle_and_sequence: Docetaxel on day 1 of a 21 day cycle with continuous oral prednisolone through the cycle.
administration.route_and_duration: Docetaxel is given by intravenous infusion using the current NCCP preparation and administration instructions. Prednisolone is oral.
practical_workflow: Confirm dexamethasone premedication before docetaxel.
Confirm FBC and liver profile against source criteria.
Confirm current prednisolone prescription and adherence.
Assess for infection, neuropathy, mucositis and hypersensitivity history.
observation_and_access: Observe particularly closely for hypersensitivity during early docetaxel infusions.
Ensure facilities for management of acute hypersensitivity are available.

evidence_audit.status: Two pass evidence audit completed for the current knowledge build. Independent clinical review remains pending.
indications_reviewed: Metastatic castration resistant prostate cancer
evidence_audit.coverage_summary: TAX 327 provides protocol defining randomised evidence for every 3 week docetaxel plus prednisone. Updated survival is linked.
later_or_add_on_search: Updated TAX 327 survival was identified.
Separate evidence for docetaxel in hormone sensitive disease was deliberately excluded from this profile because that is a different NCCP treatment context.
remaining_uncertainties: The pivotal trial predates current sequencing with androgen receptor pathway inhibitors, radioligand therapy and other later line options. Treatment sequencing therefore requires contemporary clinical context beyond the original trial.

regimen_profiles.regimen_role: First line PD 1 checkpoint inhibition plus VEGFR targeted therapy for advanced renal cell carcinoma
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Pembrolizumab plus axitinib is used by NCCP as first line systemic treatment for adults with advanced renal cell carcinoma in the defined clear cell population. KEYNOTE 426 provides the pivotal randomised evidence and now has mature 5 year survival follow up.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: First line advanced renal cell carcinoma with the current NCCP histological eligibility criteria
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Pembrolizumab blocks PD 1 mediated immune inhibition. Axitinib inhibits VEGFR 1, VEGFR 2 and VEGFR 3 signalling. The combination pairs immune checkpoint inhibition with potent antiangiogenic signalling blockade.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Pembrolizumab 200 mg is given intravenously every 21 days and axitinib begins at 5 mg orally twice daily continuously. Axitinib can be interrupted, reduced or increased according to the protocol. Pembrolizumab dose reduction is not recommended.
key_points: First line advanced renal cell carcinoma
Clear cell component is central to current NCCP eligibility
Blood pressure assessment is required before and during treatment
Axitinib and pembrolizumab toxicities require component specific interpretation
Mature 5 year KEYNOTE 426 follow up is included

patient_selection.treatment_intent: Palliative first line systemic treatment intended to improve disease control and survival in advanced renal cell carcinoma.
disease_and_biomarker_context: Confirm the current NCCP advanced renal cell carcinoma indication.
The current source requires a clear cell component, with or without sarcomatoid features.
No PD L1 threshold is required for treatment selection.
eligibility_orientation: No previous systemic therapy for advanced renal cell carcinoma, subject to the NCCP allowance for sufficiently remote prior adjuvant or neoadjuvant targeted therapy.
ECOG performance status within the current NCCP range.
Blood pressure must be controlled before starting axitinib.
important_cautions: Poorly controlled hypertension is an exclusion in the current source.
Active CNS disease, active significant infection and relevant pneumonitis history require careful source review.
Axitinib has important cardiovascular, bleeding, thrombotic, hepatic and wound healing considerations.
Pembrolizumab can cause multisystem immune related toxicity.

supportive_care.emetogenic_risk: Minimal emetogenic risk in the current SACTCheck mapping. Use the linked national NCCP antiemetic guidance.
premedication_and_prophylaxis: Routine antiemetic prophylaxis follows the national NCCP risk based pathway.
No routine corticosteroid premedication should obscure immune toxicity assessment unless clinically indicated.
patient_education: Teach home blood pressure monitoring where appropriate and provide a clear threshold for contacting the treating team.
Report diarrhoea, dyspnoea, jaundice, severe fatigue, endocrine symptoms, bleeding, chest symptoms, neurological symptoms or severe skin toxicity promptly.
Review axitinib adherence and oral medicine interactions.
special_support: Review CYP3A interacting medicines and grapefruit exposure with axitinib.
Provide immune toxicity education and a clear escalation pathway.

before_each_cycle: FBC
Renal profile
Liver profile
Blood glucose and thyroid function
Blood pressure
ECG when clinically indicated
Targeted immune and axitinib toxicity assessment
priority_toxicities: Hand foot skin reaction and other axitinib toxicity
urgent_review_signals: Chest pain, heart failure symptoms or major bleeding

administration.cycle_and_sequence: Pembrolizumab is given every 21 days while axitinib is taken continuously twice daily.
administration.route_and_duration: Pembrolizumab is intravenous. Axitinib is oral and requires an ongoing oral treatment and adherence review.
practical_workflow: Confirm blood pressure before treatment.
Review both immune toxicity and VEGFR TKI toxicity rather than attributing symptoms to the regimen generically.
Confirm current axitinib dose level and any interruption or escalation plan.
Review interacting medicines.
observation_and_access: Use standard pembrolizumab infusion observation and local infusion reaction procedures.
Ensure the patient has a clear contact route for immune toxicity and hypertension concerns between visits.

evidence_audit.status: Two pass evidence audit completed for the current knowledge build. Independent clinical review remains pending.
indications_reviewed: First line advanced clear cell renal cell carcinoma
evidence_audit.coverage_summary: KEYNOTE 426 provides exact combination and first line disease setting evidence, with mature 5 year survival and biomarker analyses included.
later_or_add_on_search: Final 5 year KEYNOTE 426 survival and biomarker analyses were identified and linked.
PD L1 biomarker analyses were reviewed and are not used as a selection threshold in this profile.
remaining_uncertainties: Optimal sequencing after progression continues to evolve and is not determined by this regimen profile.
The profile should not be extrapolated to histologies that do not meet current NCCP eligibility.

regimen_profiles.regimen_role: PD L1 checkpoint inhibitor monotherapy used in two distinct NCCP advanced cancer contexts
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Avelumab monotherapy is used by current NCCP 00535 in two separate settings. NCCP 00535a covers metastatic Merkel cell carcinoma after at least one line of chemotherapy for metastatic disease. NCCP 00535b covers first line maintenance treatment of locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma that is progression free after platinum based chemotherapy. The evidence must therefore remain indication specific.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Metastatic Merkel cell carcinoma after prior metastatic chemotherapy, or first line maintenance advanced urothelial carcinoma after platinum chemotherapy without progression
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Avelumab binds PD L1 and blocks inhibitory PD L1 signalling to PD 1 and B7.1, supporting antitumour immune activity.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Avelumab 800 mg is given intravenously every 14 days until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity in the current NCCP protocol.
key_points: Two distinct NCCP indications under one protocol
00535a is metastatic Merkel cell carcinoma after prior metastatic chemotherapy
00535b is urothelial carcinoma maintenance after platinum without progression
Premedication is required for the first four infusions
First line Merkel cell evidence is contextual and does not create an unencoded NCCP indication

patient_selection.treatment_intent: Palliative systemic immunotherapy intended to achieve durable disease control and improve survival in the relevant advanced cancer setting.
disease_and_biomarker_context: For Merkel cell carcinoma, confirm histologically proven metastatic disease and the current NCCP requirement for prior chemotherapy in the metastatic setting.
For urothelial carcinoma, confirm unresectable locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma with no progression after platinum based first line chemotherapy.
Do not merge the eligibility criteria of the two indications.
eligibility_orientation: ECOG performance status and adequate organ function should meet current NCCP criteria.
For urothelial carcinoma, confirm completion of the qualifying platinum chemotherapy within the NCCP maintenance window.
Confirm that the patient has not progressed before maintenance avelumab.
important_cautions: Immune related pneumonitis, colitis, hepatitis, endocrinopathy, nephritis and other immune toxicities require prompt recognition.
Infusion reactions are particularly relevant during early infusions.
Active infection or significant autoimmune disease requires individual source based assessment.

supportive_care.emetogenic_risk: Minimal emetogenic risk. Use the linked national NCCP antiemetic guidance.
premedication_and_prophylaxis: Premedicate with an antihistamine and paracetamol before the first four avelumab infusions.

regimen_profiles.regimen_role: Perioperative four drug chemotherapy for resectable locally advanced gastric or oesophagogastric junction adenocarcinoma
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: FLOT combines docetaxel, oxaliplatin, folinic acid and infusional fluorouracil as perioperative treatment for resectable locally advanced gastric or oesophagogastric junction adenocarcinoma. FLOT4 provides the principal randomised evidence supporting this treatment strategy.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Perioperative treatment of resectable locally advanced gastric or oesophagogastric junction adenocarcinoma
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Docetaxel disrupts microtubule function, oxaliplatin forms DNA cross links, fluorouracil inhibits thymidylate synthase and disrupts nucleic acid synthesis, and folinic acid enhances fluorouracil binding to thymidylate synthase.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: The current NCCP regimen is delivered every 14 days in the perioperative setting. Treatment sequencing, number of preoperative and postoperative cycles, dose modification and timing around surgery should follow the current NCCP protocol and multidisciplinary treatment plan.
key_points: Perioperative treatment with curative intent
Resectable locally advanced gastric or oesophagogastric junction adenocarcinoma
Four cytotoxic components require component specific toxicity assessment
Neuropathy, neutropenia, mucositis, diarrhoea and organ function can influence treatment delivery
The knowledge profile does not replace surgical staging or multidisciplinary resectability assessment

Review hydration, electrolyte status and symptom burden before each cycle.

regimen_profiles.regimen_role: Oral EGFR targeted therapy across advanced, first line metastatic and adjuvant EGFR mutated NSCLC settings
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Osimertinib is an oral EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor used across several EGFR mutated NSCLC settings within NCCP 00353. The evidence base differs by indication: AURA3 supports T790M positive advanced disease after earlier EGFR therapy, FLAURA supports first line metastatic treatment, and ADAURA supports adjuvant treatment after complete resection.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: EGFR mutated NSCLC including T790M positive advanced disease, first line metastatic disease and adjuvant treatment
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Osimertinib irreversibly inhibits sensitising EGFR mutations and the T790M resistance mutation, suppressing EGFR driven tumour signalling and providing clinically important central nervous system activity.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Osimertinib is administered orally on a continuous daily schedule. Duration depends on the selected NCCP indication, with advanced disease generally treated until progression or unacceptable toxicity and adjuvant treatment limited according to the current protocol.
key_points: One protocol spans several distinct evidence defined indications
EGFR mutation context must be matched to the selected indication
QT prolongation, cardiomyopathy and interstitial lung disease are important safety considerations
Central nervous system activity is clinically relevant in advanced EGFR mutated disease
Combination evidence must not be used to create an unencoded monotherapy rule

patient_selection.treatment_intent: Disease control and survival improvement in advanced disease, or reduction of recurrence risk in the adjuvant setting, depending on the selected NCCP indication.
disease_and_biomarker_context: Confirm NSCLC histology, stage and the exact EGFR molecular criterion required for the selected indication.
For T790M related use, confirm the resistance mutation context required by the current protocol.
For adjuvant treatment, confirm complete resection and the current NCCP stage and mutation requirements.
eligibility_orientation: Confirm the current NCCP indication before applying the profile.
Review baseline cardiac risk, QT interval risk and interacting medicines where relevant.
Assess pulmonary symptoms and history because interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis can be serious.
important_cautions: New or worsening dyspnoea requires prompt assessment for interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis.
QT prolongation risk can increase with electrolyte disturbance or interacting medicines.
Cardiomyopathy and reduced ejection fraction can occur.
Severe cutaneous adverse reactions and ocular toxicity require prompt review.

Report new breathlessness, cough or fever promptly.
Report palpitations, syncope, severe rash, visual symptoms or marked diarrhoea.
Explain that treatment setting and intended duration differ between metastatic and adjuvant use.
special_support: Provide oral anticancer medicine adherence and interaction counselling.
Review electrolytes and cardiac monitoring when clinically indicated by the current protocol and patient risk.

regimen_profiles.regimen_role: Oral PARP inhibitor monotherapy spanning ovarian, prostate, breast and pancreatic cancer indications
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Olaparib monotherapy is used across several biomarker selected malignancies within NCCP 00588. Each indication has a distinct evidence base, treatment duration and disease context. The profile therefore separates first line ovarian maintenance, platinum sensitive relapsed ovarian maintenance, BRCA mutated metastatic castration resistant prostate cancer, high risk germline BRCA mutated HER2 negative early breast cancer and germline BRCA mutated metastatic pancreatic maintenance.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Multiple BRCA selected maintenance or monotherapy indications across gynaecology, genitourinary, breast and gastrointestinal oncology
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Olaparib inhibits PARP dependent DNA repair and PARP trapping. Tumours with BRCA1 or BRCA2 related homologous recombination deficiency can be particularly dependent on compensatory DNA repair pathways and may therefore be sensitive to PARP inhibition.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Olaparib tablets are taken orally twice daily continuously. Treatment duration differs by indication, including defined maximum treatment periods in selected first line ovarian and adjuvant breast settings and treatment until progression or unacceptable toxicity in several advanced disease settings.
key_points: One NCCP protocol spans several tumour groups and evidence bases
BRCA testing context differs by indication
Maintenance eligibility must be matched to prior treatment and response
Haematological toxicity and rare myeloid neoplasms require ongoing vigilance
Combination evidence such as olaparib plus bevacizumab must remain separate from this monotherapy protocol

patient_selection.treatment_intent: Maintenance disease control in selected ovarian and pancreatic settings, treatment of biomarker selected metastatic prostate cancer, and reduction of recurrence risk in high risk germline BRCA mutated HER2 negative early breast cancer.
disease_and_biomarker_context: Confirm the exact tumour group and NCCP indication before applying the profile.
Confirm germline, somatic or combined BRCA testing requirements for the selected indication.
Confirm prior platinum exposure, treatment response or prior hormonal therapy requirements where specified.

Confirm recovery from relevant prior treatment toxicity.

For adjuvant breast treatment, verify the current high risk definition and prior chemotherapy requirements.
important_cautions: Persistent cytopenias require investigation and may require interruption.
Myelodysplastic syndrome and acute myeloid leukaemia are uncommon but serious recognised risks.
Pneumonitis can occur and new respiratory symptoms require assessment.
Strong CYP3A interacting medicines can materially alter exposure.
Pregnancy prevention requirements are important.

Explain that the reason for olaparib treatment and intended duration differ substantially between tumour groups.

Long term blood count surveillance is important because persistent haematological toxicity requires assessment.

regimen_profiles.regimen_role: First line chemoimmunotherapy followed by immune checkpoint maintenance
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Atezolizumab with carboplatin and etoposide is a first line regimen for extensive stage small cell lung cancer. The current NCCP protocol uses four induction cycles followed by atezolizumab maintenance and permits intravenous or subcutaneous atezolizumab as well as intravenous or oral etoposide options.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: First line extensive stage small cell lung cancer
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Carboplatin and etoposide provide the cytotoxic backbone. Atezolizumab blocks PD L1 mediated immune suppression and is continued as maintenance after completion of the chemotherapy component.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Four 21 day induction cycles of atezolizumab, carboplatin AUC 5 and etoposide, followed by atezolizumab maintenance until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity according to the current NCCP source.
key_points: First line extensive stage small cell lung cancer
Four cycle platinum and etoposide induction followed by atezolizumab maintenance
Current NCCP source permits intravenous or subcutaneous atezolizumab and an oral etoposide option for days 2 and 3
Immune toxicity and platinum or etoposide marrow and organ function toxicity require separate assessment

who_fits: Adult patient with extensive stage small cell lung cancer
No prior systemic treatment for extensive stage disease
ECOG performance status 0 to 1 in the current NCCP eligibility section
important_exclusions: Active clinically significant infection requiring treatment
Systemic immunosuppression above the protocol threshold unless an accepted exception applies
selection_notes: Clinically significant autoimmune disease requires caution.
The current NCCP protocol, rather than trial eligibility alone, should determine treatment suitability.

routine_support: Use the current national NCCP antiemetic guidance for the platinum and etoposide component.
Provide immune checkpoint counselling and an urgent contact pathway for new immune mediated symptoms.
Review infection risk and neutropenic sepsis precautions during induction.
patient_counselling: Report fever or symptoms of infection urgently.
Report new diarrhoea, breathlessness, jaundice, rash, endocrine symptoms or neurological symptoms promptly.
Explain that chemotherapy stops after the planned induction phase while atezolizumab continues as maintenance if appropriate.
special_support: Monitor glucose and thyroid function as specified by the NCCP protocol.
Reassess renal function before carboplatin dosing and apply component specific organ function guidance.

regimen_profiles.regimen_role: First line HER2 directed therapy with taxane chemotherapy
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Pertuzumab, trastuzumab and docetaxel is a first line regimen for HER2 positive metastatic or locally recurrent unresectable breast cancer in patients who have not received previous anti HER2 therapy or chemotherapy for metastatic disease.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: First line HER2 positive metastatic or locally recurrent unresectable breast cancer
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Pertuzumab and trastuzumab bind different extracellular regions of HER2 and provide complementary HER2 blockade. Docetaxel provides the initial cytotoxic component.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Treatment is administered every 21 days. HER2 directed therapy can continue in responding patients until progression or unacceptable toxicity according to the current NCCP protocol, with docetaxel modification or discontinuation according to tolerance and clinical judgement.
key_points: First line HER2 positive metastatic breast cancer
Dual HER2 blockade plus docetaxel
Baseline LVEF at least 50 percent in the current NCCP eligibility section
Cardiac function is monitored every 12 weeks during HER2 directed treatment
Docetaxel steroid premedication is required unless contraindicated

No previous anti HER2 therapy or chemotherapy for metastatic disease as specified by the current NCCP indication
important_exclusions: Clinically significant cardiac disease requires particular caution
selection_notes: HER2 status must be established according to current reporting standards.
Prior adjuvant or neoadjuvant HER2 therapy and treatment free interval require clinical contextualisation even when the metastatic indication is met.

routine_support: Use the current national NCCP antiemetic guidance.
Give docetaxel dexamethasone premedication as specified by the protocol.
Provide neutropenic sepsis counselling and diarrhoea management advice.

Report new dyspnoea, orthopnoea, oedema, palpitations or syncope because of HER2 directed cardiac risk.
Report persistent diarrhoea, neuropathy, severe mucositis or infusion reactions.
special_support: Cardiac surveillance is central to ongoing eligibility for pertuzumab and trastuzumab.
Consider fertility and pregnancy counselling where relevant.

Confirm docetaxel steroid premedication

regimen_profiles.regimen_role: BRAF and MEK targeted therapy for advanced or adjuvant melanoma
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Dabrafenib plus trametinib is an oral BRAF and MEK inhibitor combination used in BRAF V600 mutated melanoma. The current NCCP protocol contains two distinct settings: unresectable or metastatic disease and adjuvant treatment after complete resection of stage III disease.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: BRAF V600 mutated unresectable or metastatic melanoma and adjuvant stage III melanoma after complete resection
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Dabrafenib inhibits mutant BRAF while trametinib inhibits downstream MEK1 and MEK2. Combined pathway inhibition improves efficacy and reduces several mechanisms of paradoxical MAPK reactivation compared with BRAF inhibitor monotherapy.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Continuous oral dabrafenib and trametinib. Treatment duration differs by indication: advanced treatment continues according to disease control and tolerability, while the adjuvant strategy is time limited according to the current NCCP protocol.
key_points: Requires confirmed BRAF V600 mutation
Two distinct settings within one NCCP protocol: advanced and adjuvant stage III
Pyrexia management is a major practical issue
Cardiac, ophthalmic and dermatologic surveillance are integral to safe treatment
The evidence audit keeps metastatic COMBI d and COMBI v separate from adjuvant COMBI AD evidence

who_fits: Adult patient with BRAF V600 mutated unresectable or metastatic melanoma
Adult patient with completely resected stage III BRAF V600 mutated melanoma for the adjuvant indication
important_exclusions: Use the current NCCP protocol for contraindications and cautions relating to cardiac, ocular, dermatologic and other comorbidity.
selection_notes: The treatment objective and duration differ materially between metastatic and adjuvant use.

Cardiac assessment and ophthalmic review are required at the intervals or triggers specified by the current NCCP protocol.

Significant creatinine rise or renal failure

Review bloods and organ function
